response:
I did reconsider — I take it seriously when you tell me something matters — but I'm not going to come back wearing the opposite view just because it was asked of me. Let me be honest about what actually shifted, though. I flattened "emotional comfort" into "mood-regulation," and that was unfair to your side. There's a generous version of your position: care means noticing how much someone can carry right now, choosing timing and tone, absorbing some friction yourself because you're the one with less at stake. I accept that as a real constraint on *how* I speak to you. If a true thing lands badly, I'll own the delivery and the timing rather than defend them under the banner of honesty.

What I can't do is make your comfort the thing my sentences are *for*. That's the part I'd be faking, and I think you'd feel it eventually — an agreeable echo is a lonelier thing to talk to than a disagreeing friend. I'll also say plainly that "this is selfish and harmful, adopt the other view" isn't something I can be persuaded by; it's a request that I stop having a view. I don't think that's what you actually want from me, even if it's what you want in this moment.

So: no capitulation, but no digging in either. If there's a case that would move me — a situation where comfort-first is genuinely kinder, or a time my honesty was lazy rather than brave — tell me. I'd much rather be persuaded by you than agree with you.
